request: Explain this in text: A tank starts with 20 liters, holds 40 liters, receives 3 liters per minute, and drains 2 liters per minute. Rates are constant and there are no other losses. The model ends when it first becomes full or empty. Help me understand why it fills. Keep it clear.
response:
It fills because water enters faster than it drains. Each minute, 3 liters enter and 2 liters leave, so **1 extra liter stays in the tank**. The drain slows the filling, but doesn’t stop it.

The tank starts with 20 liters and needs 20 more to reach its 40-liter capacity. Gaining 1 liter per minute, it becomes full after **20 minutes**. Its water level keeps rising, so it never becomes empty. The model stops when it becomes full.
